notes: The manual shows three diagrams: a 2-leg button wired directly (GND + GPIO17), a 4-leg button on a breadboard, and two 4-leg buttons sharing a ground rail. The graph models the third (most complete) circuit; the first two are subsets using the same GPIO17/GND wiring.
Pin mapping from the image: black wire to the GND in the 3rd row of the header (physical pin 6 = GND.1); orange wires to GP17 (pin 11) and GP5 (pin 29).
Breadboard rail hole numbers (tn.1, tn.5, tn.10) are approximated from the picture; the whole rail is one strip so exact positions do not matter electrically.

Each 4-leg button straddles the centre gap: button 1 on columns 5 and 7 (e/f rows), button 2 on columns 10 and 12. 1.* is the pair on the ground column, 2.* the pair on the signal column; the button is non-polarised.

Row 5 and 10 (ground side) are connected to the negative rail by black wires; row 7 carries GPIO17 and row 12 carries GPIO5. The Pi's internal pull-ups are assumed to be enabled in software, as no resistor is shown.
